name: Rust Grunt
description: The one enemy type the GDD asks for first: a Rust security officer in a slate uniform with a steel helmet and a cyan visor. Symmetrical, boxy and cold, a sharp contrast to Zed's warm, rounded look. Lore: the Rust strip recruits of their names and give them serial numbers, so the helmets hide who is under them on purpose; many were ordinary citizens coerced or manipulated into service.
behaviour: Idles briefly after spawn, then chases Zed. Closes the lane gap first, and starts a strike once in range. At most two grunts may attack at once (attacker cap); the rest circle at a distance in neutral colours until a slot frees up. GDD move list (Iron Line grunts): Rust Jab Combo, a quick 1-2-3 punch string of light damage, used to interrupt the player and often done in groups to create pressure; and Helmet Headbutt, a sudden forward lunge with a reinforced helmet, short wind-up, brief stun, used when Zed is too close or grabs too often. The Tier 0 engine implements the single strike only; the jab combo and headbutt are later-tier additions to gruntData.js and need the combat contract to support multi-hit strings and a stun hit.
telegraph: 450 ms wind-up: three-frame anticipation pose with the arm pulled back, the red telegraph icon pops above the head, the body tints red and the outline thickens. Then a quick 250 ms strike and a 700 ms recovery where it is open to a counter.
weakness: Low health and a slow recovery. Dodge or block the telegraphed strike, then punish during recovery with a light combo.
look: Slate uniform, steel helmet, cyan visor, cheap oxidized plating kept to cold slate tones; boxy and symmetrical, no personal marks (serial-number recruits).
